verdicts.quote: No line compares `max` with a configured maximum, with len(m), or with anything else the client does not choose.
verdicts.why: N03 is the advisory by mechanism, not merely by neighbourhood. It names the same sink (sliceMapToSlice, openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go), the same attacker-controlled input (the bracketed decimal index of a deepObject query key, taken from the query string unmodified via DecodeObject -> makeObject -> buildResObj), the same allocation rule (strconv.Atoi on the key, `max` = largest key seen, then `for i := 0; i <= max; i++ { result = append(result, ...) }`, plus the second `make([]any, len(arr))` at :986), and the same absence of any bound. It states explicitly that the work happens 'before a single schema keyword is evaluated', which is the advisory's decisive clause that maxItems never gets to apply, and it gives the same exploit shape: an unauthenticated ~30-byte query string turning into ~2e9 iterations and tens of gigabytes, ending in OOM. Location openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:936 matches the advisory's own cited line. Other findings in this batch sit in the same package or the same decoder but are different defects (N06 zip decompression/append bug, N02 nil RegexMatcher panic, N01 per-request recompile CPU cost) and none of them was needed to reach this verdict.
